dicas.texto: Você sabe o que acontece com uma fração quando o numerador é maior que o denominador? O que isso nos diz sobre a posição dela em relação ao número 1?
Tente dividir cada unidade inteira (de 0 a 1 e de 1 a 2) em 9 partes iguais. Onde o décimo pedaço cairia?
Como você tem 10 pedaços de 1/9, você vai passar do primeiro inteiro. Conte 9 pedaços até o 1 e adicione mais um depois dele.
Se 9/9 é exatamente o 1, o 10/9 está apenas um pequeno passo à direita do número 1 na reta numérica.

passos.acao: Divide Dale's number line into 9 equal parts and confirm.
Mark Dale's amount, 10/9, on the first number line.
Divide Liz's number line into 1 equal part and confirm.
Mark Liz's amount, 1 pound, on the second number line.
Compare the two marked points and indicate their positional relationship.
Select the sauce with more ground beef, then click Done.

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number line?
Use the denominator of Dale's fraction to decide how many equal intervals to create.
Look at the bottom number in Dale's fraction, 10/9.
Enter the denominator shown in 10/9, then confirm the division.
Compare the numerator and denominator before locating the point.
Count ninths from 0, passing the point for 1 when you reach 9/9.
The point for 1 is 9/9, so the next ninth is just beyond 1.
Start at 0, count ten equal ninth intervals, and place the marker at the tenth interval.
How many equal parts are needed to represent one whole?
Write 1 pound as a fraction with one whole part.
A whole number can be written with a denominator of 1.
Enter the denominator in the fraction 1/1, then confirm.
Where is one whole located on a number line from 0 to 2?
Use the endpoints and the equal interval to locate one whole.
The point halfway between 0 and 2 is the mark for 1.
Start at 0 and move one whole interval to the right before placing the marker.
On a number line, which point represents the greater amount?
Compare the locations of the two markers from left to right.
Remember that 10/9 contains one whole and one additional ninth.
Look at the marker that lies farther right and name that direction.
Which sauce has the marker farther to the right on the number line?
Rewrite Liz's whole pound as ninths so both amounts use the same-sized parts.
One pound is 9/9, while Dale has 10/9.
Choose the sauce whose amount has the greater numerator when both amounts are written in ninths, then click Done.

exercicio.statement:
Dale and Liz are each making their own spaghetti sauce, and are using different amounts of ground beef to make it. If you wanted your sauce to have more ground beef, whose sauce should you choose? Use the number line to find out.
Dale is using 10/9 pounds of ground beef.
Liz is using exactly 1 pound of ground beef.
Which sauce should you choose?

steps.instruction: Divide Dale's number line into 9 equal parts and confirm.
Mark Dale's amount, 10/9, on the first number line.
Divide Liz's number line into 1 equal part and confirm.
Mark Liz's amount, 1 pound, on the second number line.
Compare the two marked points and indicate their positional relationship.
Select the sauce with more ground beef, then click Done.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas em vez dos intervalos, resultando em uma divisão a menos
misconceptions.feedback: You counted marks instead of intervals. To make 9 equal parts, count the spaces between the marks.

misconceptions.description: O aluno confunde o valor total da fração com o denominador da reta
misconceptions.feedback: You used the numerator, 10, instead of the denominator. The denominator is the bottom number in 10/9 and tells how many equal parts to make.

misconceptions.description: O aluno começa a contar a partir do primeiro traço como se fosse o 1, deslocando o ponto
misconceptions.feedback: You started counting from the first mark as if it were 1. Begin at 0, then count ten ninth intervals.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ancora o valor na metade da reta (0.5 ou 1) por não saber localizar frações
misconceptions.feedback: You placed the point at the middle of the line instead of locating ten ninths. Since 10/9 is greater than 1, its point must be just beyond 1.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ignora a necessidade de dividir a reta quando a fração é um inteiro
misconceptions.feedback: You did not create a division for the whole. Even 1 pound can be represented as 1/1, so the denominator is 1.

misconceptions.feedback: You counted the first mark as an extra step. Begin at 0 and move one whole interval to reach 1.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ancora o valor na metade da reta (0.5 ou 1) por não saber localizar frações
misconceptions.feedback: You marked half of one instead of one whole. Liz's amount is exactly 1 pound.

misconceptions.description: O aluno julga a fração pela diferença para o inteiro (gap)
misconceptions.feedback: You focused on how close each amount is to the next whole number. Since 10/9 is already greater than 1, Dale's point is farther right.

misconceptions.description: O aluno usa a lógica de quanto falta para o inteiro (gap) para comparar frações
misconceptions.feedback: You compared the distance to the next whole instead of the amounts themselves. A numerator greater than its denominator means 10/9 is greater than 1.

misconceptions.description: O aluno compara apenas os numeradores, ignorando o significado da fração
misconceptions.feedback: You treated the numerator and the whole number as if they were directly comparable. Rewrite 1 as 9/9, then compare it with 10/9.
